terms.meaning: A want backed by willingness and ability to pay: the quantity bought at a given price and time.
The quantity of goods and services ready for sale at a given price.
Using goods and services to satisfy wants.
The power to satisfy a want. It can't be measured and varies by person, time and place.
Value expressed in money: what is paid for a good or service.
The total money value of all goods and services a country produces in a year.

items.name: Demand and price
items.formula: When price rises, demand usually falls.
items.example: Demand is called the index of a nation's progress.

items.name: Supply and price
items.formula: When price rises, supply usually rises too.
items.example: In some cases supply stays the same whatever the price.

items.name: Two pillars of economic activity
items.formula: Demand and supply: a change in one quickly affects the other, seen in the price.
items.example: Price's main job is to make demand equal supply.

items.name: Meaning of production
items.formula: Man can't create anything new, only add utility to what nature gives.
items.example: It is complete only when goods reach the consumer.

items.name: Factors of production and their rewards
items.formula: Land, labour, capital and organisation get rent, wages, interest and profit.
items.example: Each is paid by the part it plays.

items.name: Two types of consumption
items.formula: Goods used to make other goods, and finished goods used to satisfy wants.
items.example: More consumption means more production, income and jobs.

items.name: Profit
items.formula: What the producer keeps after paying rent, wages and interest.

items.name: Form utility
items.formula: Gained by giving a thing a new shape.
items.example: A sculptor's idol from stone; a carpenter's chair from wood.

items.name: Time utility
items.formula: Gained by storing a thing until it is scarce.
items.example: Mango pickle eaten when mangoes are out of season.

items.name: Place utility
items.formula: Gained by moving a thing to where it isn't grown.
items.example: Shimla apples or Kodagu oranges sold far away.

items.name: Per capita income
items.example: ₹1000 crore shared by 10 lakh people is ₹10,000 each.

items.name: Co-operation
items.formula: People join as equals for self-help: one vote each, shared profit, no middlemen.
items.example: Its spirit: "Each for all and all for each".

items.name: Physical and mental labour
items.formula: Physical: digging, ploughing, carrying loads. Mental: teachers, scientists, lawyers, clerks.
items.example: Gandhiji believed in the dignity of all labour.

mistakes.text: Utility isn't the same as usefulness: alcohol has no use but has utility, because it satisfies a want.
Utility is the power to satisfy; satisfaction is its effect.
Per capita income is national income divided by population, so a rich nation with a huge population can still have low per capita income.
